export_controls.description: $39B manufacturing subsidies + $13B R&D. Recipients barred from expanding chip fabs in China for 10 years. 25% investment tax credit for US fab construction.
First sweeping controls blocking A100-class+ chips to China. Introduced TPP and performance-density thresholds. Also restricted semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
Japan restricted 23 types of advanced chip manufacturing equipment (lithography, etching, deposition). Expanded by 21 items in Apr 2024. China stockpiled $5B in equipment pre-deadline.

China imposed export licenses on gallium and germanium. Escalated to graphite (Oct 2023), antimony (Aug 2024), tungsten (Feb 2025), rare earths (Apr 2025). Full US halt Dec 2024. Partially suspended Nov 2025 under trade truce.
Blocked ASML from selling advanced DUV immersion lithography to China. Expanded Sep 2024 to require licenses for 1970i/1980i DUV machines. ASML China revenue projected to drop from 29% to ~20%.
Closed loopholes — blocked A800/H800 China workaround variants. Added performance-density thresholds capturing RTX 4090 gaming GPU. Expanded Entity List.
NVIDIA released downgraded H20 and L20 chips designed to comply with US thresholds for the China market. Reduced memory bandwidth and compute performance vs H100.

export_controls.target: EU + any entity selling AI in EU
export_controls.description: World's first comprehensive AI law. Risk-based framework: prohibited/high/limited/minimal risk tiers. Penalties up to EUR 35M or 7% global turnover. Phase 1 (prohibited practices) Feb 2025, Phase 2 (GPAI) Aug 2025, Phase 3 (high-risk) Aug 2026.

export_controls.regulation: Biden Entity List + HBM Controls + FDPR Expansion
export_controls.description: Added 140 entities to Entity List (fabs, tool makers, Huawei suppliers). First country-wide HBM export controls to China. Expanded Foreign Direct Product Rule scope. Restricted advanced AI chip packaging tech.

3-tier global system: Tier 1 (18 allies) unrestricted; Tier 2 (~150 countries) quantity caps ~50K GPUs/entity; Tier 3 (~25 countries incl. China) prohibited. Also controlled AI model weights. Rescinded by Trump admin May 2025 before compliance date.

export_controls.regulation: EU AI Act Phase 1 — Prohibited Practices
export_controls.description: Ban on social scoring, emotion recognition in workplaces/schools, untargeted facial scraping, predictive crime assessment. First enforcement phase of EU AI Act.
Eliminated Biden's 3-tier country system and quantity caps 2 days before compliance date. Replaced with bilateral deal-based approach. Pre-existing China entity-level controls remain.
Declared using/selling/servicing Huawei Ascend 910B/C/D chips anywhere violates US export controls under Foreign Direct Product Rule. Extraterritorial worldwide scope.
Draft BIS rule requiring export licenses for AI GPU shipments to Malaysia/Thailand — evidence of transshipment to China. Enhanced documentation and end-use verification.
Export license for NVIDIA/AMD to sell H20-class chips to China with 15% of China sales revenue paid to US government. First-ever revenue-sharing arrangement tied to export licenses.

export_controls.regulation: EU AI Act Phase 2 — GPAI Obligations
export_controls.description: General-Purpose AI model obligations take effect. AI Office becomes operational. Compute reporting requirements for GPAI providers. Governance infrastructure established.
Commerce authorized 70,000 NVIDIA GB300 chips to HUMAIN (Saudi) and G42 (UAE). Ended regulatory standoff blocking billions in data center investments. Part of US-Gulf AI partnership.
China suspended export controls on gallium, germanium, antimony, graphite, and rare earths for 1 year under trade truce. General licenses issued for US end users. Can be reimposed at any time.

export_controls.regulation: Trump H200 to China (25% Revenue Share)
export_controls.description: Authorized NVIDIA H200 sales to vetted Chinese customers with 25% revenue share to US government (up from 15% for H20). Near-cutting-edge chips to China under commercial terms. Bipartisan criticism.
First SE Asian comprehensive AI law. Phased implementation starting Mar 2026 over 4 years. Establishes AI governance framework for Vietnamese market.

Codified shift from 'presumption of denial' to 'case-by-case review' for H200/MI325X-class exports to China. Requires: sufficient US domestic supply, no foundry capacity diversion, third-party testing, and recipient security procedures.

25% tariff on imported advanced AI semiconductors, SME, and derivative products. Broad exemptions for US data center imports, R&D, startups, consumer use, and public sector. Impact review due Jul 2026.

Congressional oversight of AI chip exports like arms sales. Creates 'Trusted US Person' framework for ally deployments. Would temporarily revoke existing China licenses pending national security strategy review. Passed committee markup Jan 2026.

ISM 2.0 expanded beyond fab subsidies to semiconductor equipment, materials, and IP. 10 approved fab projects; $38B domestic market targeting $100B by 2030. Government subsidizes AI compute at Rs 65/GPU-hr vs global $2-3/hr.

export_controls.regulation: EU AI Act Phase 3 — High-Risk AI Systems
export_controls.description: Full compliance for high-risk standalone AI systems: biometrics, critical infrastructure, employment, law enforcement, education, migration. Conformity assessments and CE marking required.

basis_legend.measured: Read from a live external source this run.
basis_legend.reference: Curated from published documents; refreshed manually.
basis_legend.modeled: Estimate. No public source exists for these numbers.
basis_legend.mixed: Contains both measured and estimated fields — see detail.

providers.detail: Live provider APIs and published price lists. Every price carries a source and last_verified; nothing is published without one.

matrix.detail: Recomputed from providers + specs on each run.

spot.detail: Aggregated from provider prices. bid/ask are a modelled spread around the live average, not a traded quote.

historical.detail: Monthly snapshots of the provider average.

summary.detail: Recomputed from matrix, providers and indicators.

workload_recs.detail: Prices re-derived from live provider listings; GPU shortlists are editorial.

tco.detail: Cloud rates track live provider averages; power/colo/staff inputs are industry-typical assumptions you can override in the Scenario Builder.

reservations.detail: Rates track live provider averages; breakeven maths assumes the commitment is paid for every hour of the term.

forecasts.detail: Statistical projection from price history. Not a measurement and not investment advice.

inference.detail: OpenRouter rankings (weekly token volume) + /api/v1/models for pricing and context. Parameter counts are vendor-published where disclosed, else marked estimated.

news.detail: Google News RSS. Dates are as published.

sentiment.detail: Reddit, HuggingFace and GitHub APIs. Composite scores are our own weighting.

indicators.detail: Stock prices are live (Yahoo Finance). Market size and AI capex are derived from reported company revenue and guidance. Shipment counts are estimates.

competitive.detail: Market shares from published revenue and analyst estimates; scores (performance, moat, ecosystem) are our own editorial rating.

sustainability.detail: Provider sustainability reports and grid carbon intensity. Per-GPU figures computed from TDP.

supplychain.detail: Export-control timeline is public record. Vendor risk scores and regional inventory counts are estimates.

regional.detail: Regional market shares, data-centre counts and price premiums are estimates, not measured.

utilization.detail: No provider publishes per-GPU utilisation. Illustrative estimates.

modelfit.detail: Throughput and batch sizes are estimates, not benchmarked.
